Central target of the whole chapter: the Western tradition's unexamined assumption that 'being' reduces to continuous presence, obscuring the role of absence/possibility in experience (FE, p.2-9).
Heidegger's recurring topic across PM/IM/BT; what anxiety discloses as constitutive of Dasein's own being, not a 'something' that logic can rule illogical (FAITHFUL-O'Brien).
Glossed as a fundamental existentiale prior to all psychology of moods, inseparable from Dasein's basic constitution (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, p.15-16, quoting SZ 131, 134).

The 'founding mode of attunement' that reveals beings as a whole and constitutes the basic occurrence of Dasein, distinguished from directed thematic feelings (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, p.12, quoting BW 100).
Fear is always fear of a particular threatening entity; anxiety is anxious about and before nothing in particular, disclosing Being-in-the-world as such (FE, citing SZ 186, BW 100).
Names the 'that it is' of Dasein's being delivered over to its 'there,' veiled in whence/whither yet disclosed all the more unveiledly (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, p.19, quoting SZ 135).
Heidegger's explicitly stated aim for BT's Dasein-analytic, opposed to anthropology, psychology, humanism, existentialism (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, quoting SZ 131, SZ 200).
Part of what falling/absorption is disclosive evidence of; Dasein as 'the null basis of a nullity,' with underlying angst a constant testament to this (FE, p.19-20).
The temporal correlate of the anxiety analysis: Dasein is never purely present, always thrown, oriented toward the ultimate possibility of no-longer-being (FE, p.23-24).

That in the face of which one has anxiety is 'the possibility of the ready-to-hand in general... the world itself,' not any specific present-at-hand entity (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, p.24, quoting SZ 186-187).
Heidegger's own 1935 lecture-hall illustration (IM 32): the chalk's possibility of being used up belongs to what the chalk is, not something added by thought (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, p.5-7, quoting IM 32).

Husserlian illustration: we perceive a whole lamp, a three-dimensional picture, a car 'not slowing down to turn into the driveway' though bare sensation gives only partial profiles (FE, p.9-10).

Heidegger's own repeated insistence that mood-analysis serves fundamental ontology alone, against the field's persistent tendency to read Angst/Befindlichkeit as a contribution to psychology or existentialist humanism (FE).

target: logic/non-contradiction vs. meaningfulness of talk about the Nothing (DEBATE-AXIS)
note: Carnap/logical-positivist dismissal of 'the Nothing' as illogical nonsense vs. Heidegger's claim that logic's authority over the being-question is itself an unexamined, question-begging assumption (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, citing IM 25-27).
Fallenness is not counter-evidence against what bare moods disclose but evidence for it: 'in the evasion itself the "there" is something disclosed' (FAITHFUL-O'Brien, p.19, quoting SZ 135).
